title: The Paradox of Prohibition: Making Everything More Dangerous

content_html_sanitized:
Although “hard drugs” are off topic for MarijuanaNews, they offer the most extreme evidence of the paradox of prohibition. Unknown potency and/or purity can be fatal. Fentanyl is an extreme example with over 100,000 deaths in 2023.

See

Marijuana Is In Schedule One. Fentanyl Is In Schedule 2. Think About It.

 

With Cannabis, the dangers are much less obvious, with one exception, the danger of getting arrested, which can occasionally be fatal.

See

Lest We Forget: From Twenty Years Ago, July 12,2005:The Murder of Steve McWilliams. An Indictment, Not An Obituary. The Absurdity of Evil. Condolences from NORML.

 

Otherwise, the best example is using a vape pen, which can and should be the safest way to inhale cannabinoids. Unlike “smoking” or “toking”, etc, vaping a pure concentrate of known potency allows the user to control the dosage. And only with legalization can the customer know the potency (THC%), supposedly of such great concern for Prohibitionists.

 

However, when buying a vape pen in a contraband market, the old saying, “know your dealer” is more important than ever.

 

(Also knowing who you can believe.)

See

Is Vaping Cannabis Really Worse Than Vaping Tobacco for Teens’ Lungs?

 

A contraband vape pen may not even have real cannabis in it. So-called “synthetic cannabis” isn’t even cannabis at all.

See

The Problems with “Synthetic Cannabis” Begin With Its Name

And

Legalizing Alcohol Made Under Age Drinking Less Dangerous. Legal Cannabis Can Do The Same for Teens Illegally Toking and Vaping. The Dangers of Synthetic Cannabinoids

 

Otherwise, hundreds of millions of people around the world have smoked weed and/or hash, in hand rolled joints, with or without tobacco.

 

Not the healthiest way, but… tobacco is still an acceptable risk. Actually, the only known mass contamination of marijuana was done by the Nixon Administration with Paraquat

 

Ironically, after large numbers of American weed aficionados started coming to Amsterdam, Dutch smokers who smoked weed or hash with tobacco, called American style joints “pure” or “American”. Probably the only time “American” has been a synonym for “pure.”

 

There is also one more way that legalization can make weed safer, by creating value in brand names, via advertising.

See

In Defense of Cannabis Advertising

And

Feds Try To Undermine California’s Legal Marijuana Industry Vía Selective Prosecution of Advertising Companies

And

The United Nations Wants to Ban Cannabis Advertising
